{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-tn","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"a4b49416e4f56d5e06e4e1919ac462b9dec524ccbef00f4758ed4f12d11cc63a","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-tn-class-d:lineage:10","source_registry_sha256":"8b0b6a068a0aa720d419171b5007a2610ed6c5012eeff522b57713cf9226eb71","source_liveness_sha256":"d27b9a94f03ec29d960b8eea38966606a7d3fdb703ad30b19ecd93f9bc70d0c7"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Graduated driver license for drivers under eighteen","heading":"C — Intermediate licenses for drivers under eighteen: the four GDL steps, permit and intermediate rules, out-of-state teens, GDL penalties, minor documentation and teen phone laws","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Intermediate licenses for drivers under eighteen: the four GDL steps, permit and intermediate rules, out-of-state teens, GDL penalties, minor documentation and teen phone laws
Knowledge domain: how a Tennessee driver under eighteen moves from learner permit to regular license — the age, holding-period, practice-hour, curfew, passenger and points rules at each step, the penalties that delay or reverse progress, the adult and school paperwork, and the teen phone and texting laws.

FACT_ID: sec03-F01 | anchor: A01
Tennessee requires drivers under 18 to build driving experience through graduated steps before they can hold a full, unrestricted license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-F02 | anchor: A01
The four steps of the Graduated Driver License program are the Learner Permit, the Intermediate Restricted License, the Intermediate Unrestricted License and the Regular Driver License. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-F03 | anchor: A01
A license issued at any of the first three GDL steps shows GDL printed in its bottom left corner. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-F04 | anchor: A01
A learner permit requires being 15 and passing the standard written exams and the vision screening. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-F05 | anchor: A01
A teen must hold the learner permit for 180 days before moving up to the Intermediate Restricted License. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-F06 | anchor: A01
A permit holder may drive only when a licensed driver aged 21 or older rides in the front seat. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-F07 | anchor: A01
A permit holder may not drive between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-F08 | anchor: A01
The Intermediate Restricted License requires being 16 and passing the driving skills test, also called the road test. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-F09 | anchor: A01
For the Intermediate Restricted License, a parent, legal guardian or licensed driving instructor must certify fifty hours of driving practice, ten of them at night, on the Department's form SF-1256. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-F10 | anchor: A01
Moving up to the Intermediate Unrestricted License requires being 17 and having held the Intermediate Restricted License for 1 year. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-F11 | anchor: A01
The Intermediate Unrestricted License is refused after an at-fault traffic accident or 2 safety belt violations, and it needs no additional tests. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-F12 | anchor: A01
A teen can get the regular Class D license at 18 or on graduating high school or earning a GED, whichever comes first, and the license drops the word Intermediate but keeps its Under 21 markings. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-F13 | anchor: A01
A 15-year-old new resident holding a valid permit from another state qualifies only for a Tennessee learner permit and must reach 180 total days on a permit and turn 16 before the Intermediate Restricted License. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-F14 | anchor: A01
Time on the previous state's permit can count toward the 180 days if the teen shows a certified driving record issued within the 30 days before the Tennessee application. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-F15 | anchor: A02
Since July 1, 2018, every license issued to someone under 21 has been printed in a vertical format. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec03-F16 | anchor: A03
If the previous state's record shows any violation or accident, the teen keeps a Tennessee learner permit until the Driver Improvement Section confirms the record meets the less than 6 points rule. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-F17 | anchor: A03
A 16-year-old holding a valid out-of-state license issued at least 90 days before applying applies for the Intermediate Restricted License. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-F18 | anchor: A03
A teen whose out-of-state license is less than 90 days old gets the Intermediate Restricted License only with a clear record showing at least 180 combined days on a permit or license. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-F19 | anchor: A03
However long a license was held in another state, the Tennessee Intermediate Restricted License must still be held one year before the Unrestricted level. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-F20 | anchor: A03
Both intermediate levels list the license class as Class D and display Intermediate Driver License in the yellow header bar on the front. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-F21 | anchor: A03
A learner permit holder whose record reaches 6 or more points must keep the permit until the record stays under 6 points for 180 consecutive days. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-F22 | anchor: A03
A forged letter of parental approval, or contributing to a fatal accident, revokes the Intermediate Restricted License and leaves the teen with only a learner permit until age 18. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-F23 | anchor: A03
On the Intermediate Restricted License, 6 or more points, contributing to an accident, or a second seatbelt conviction adds 90 days to the one-year minimum, for one year and three months in total. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-F24 | anchor: A03
A second moving-violation conviction on the Intermediate Restricted License requires finishing a certified driver education course before advancing. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-F25 | anchor: A03
If a violation from the Intermediate Restricted period reaches the Department only after the Unrestricted license is issued, the teen drops back to Intermediate Restricted for 90 days. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-F26 | anchor: A04
Every applicant under 18 needs an adult to sign the Minor/Teenage Affidavit and Cancellation form, joining the application and accepting responsibility, including financial responsibility, for the young driver. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec03-F27 | anchor: A04
Allowed signers of the teen affidavit are a parent, foster parent or step-parent sharing the applicant's address, a legal guardian, or a grandparent whom one of those adults has authorized. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec03-F28 | anchor: A04
A graduate proves school status with an original diploma or GED certificate, while an enrolled Tennessee student brings an original SF1010 form that is valid for 30 days after the school signs it. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec03-F29 | anchor: A04
Grade cards and school transcripts are never accepted as proof of school attendance or progress. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec03-F30 | anchor: A04
A student 15 or older who drops out loses driving privileges; after the first dropout the privilege returns on going back to school, but after a second dropout the student must wait until 18 to apply. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec03-F31 | anchor: A04
A student reinstated after returning to school pays a $20 reinstatement fee on top of the application and license fees. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec03-F32 | anchor: A05
Tennessee bans any learner permit or intermediate license holder from using a cell phone, whether handheld, car phone or other mobile phone, while driving on a Tennessee road. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec03-F33 | anchor: A05
A teen convicted under the cell phone ban faces a Class C misdemeanor, a $50.00 fine, 6 points on the record and a 90-day delay in Intermediate Restricted eligibility. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec03-F34 | anchor: A05
Since July 1, 2009, texting while driving has been banned for all drivers, with a fine of no more than fifty dollars plus court costs of no more than ten dollars. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec03-F35 | anchor: A06
An Intermediate Restricted driver may carry only 1 other passenger, unless a passenger is 21 or older with a valid unrestricted license, or the passengers are siblings living in the same home and the driver carries a parent's letter for school trips. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec03-F36 | anchor: A06
An Intermediate Restricted driver may not drive from 11 p.m. to 6 a.m. unless with a parent or guardian, with a written-designated licensed driver 21 or older, going to or from a school event or work with written permission, or going hunting or fishing between 4 a.m. and 6 a.m. with a valid license. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec03-F37 | anchor: A06
Being convicted of carrying a forged or fraudulent permission letter revokes the Intermediate Restricted License and leaves only a learner permit until age 18. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec03-F38 | anchor: A06
Six points on the record is roughly the same as two minor traffic citations. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec03-F39 | anchor: A07
A 16-year-old emancipated by active-duty military service, marriage or court order may obtain a regular Class D license. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec03-F40 | anchor: A07
At the permit and both intermediate levels, seat belts are mandatory for every passenger aged 4 through 17, and a child under 4 must ride in a child restraint device. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0034]

Misconceptions: the permit curfew and the restricted-license curfew start at different hours; the Intermediate Unrestricted license still says Intermediate even though its limits are gone; out-of-state license time never shortens the Tennessee one-year restricted period; a fake permission letter does not just add time but drops the teen back to a permit.
Mnemonics: fifteen to learn, sixteen to drive restricted, seventeen to loosen up, eighteen to graduate; ten at night is the permit curfew, eleven is the restricted curfew; fifty hours with ten after dark.
Glossary: GDL means the Graduated Driver License program; Intermediate Restricted means the first post-permit level with passenger and curfew limits; Intermediate Unrestricted means the second level with no driving limits; Restriction Card means the card carried with a permit or restricted license that lists its limits; Certificate of Compulsory School Attendance means the school form that proves enrollment and satisfactory progress.
Dynamic facts: fees, form numbers, school-certificate procedures and the GDL fee table can change; confirm them on the Department of Safety and Homeland Security website before showing them to learners.
